```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("vanderHeijden_2023_alectinib"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("vanderHeijden_2023_alectinib"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.13647> (open access; the parameter
  table and NONMEM code are in the article's Data S1)

van der Heijden 2023 did not fit a model to data. It asked whether a
stable-isotope-labelled microtracer (100 ug alectinib-d6), given once with a
standardized meal and once fasted to patients already at steady state on
alectinib, could detect a 40% food effect on bioavailability. To answer it the
authors simulated microtracer concentrations with the population PK model of
the European Medicines Agency (EMA) Alecensa assessment report, to which they
added a fixed food effect on bioavailability and between-occasion variability
(IOV) on bioavailability, and then ran stochastic simulation and estimation
(1000 trials per design) in NONMEM. This package ships that simulation model.

# Population

The structural model and its estimates come from 138 patients with locally
advanced or metastatic ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer in the pooled
pivotal phase II studies NP28673 and NP28761, all of whom received alectinib
600 mg twice daily with a meal (Data S1 Table S1). Median age was 52 years
(range 22-79); 56% were female; 67% White, 26% Asian, 0.7% Black or African
American, 0.7% American Indian or Alaska Native, 3% other and 2% unknown. 61%
had CNS metastases, 95% had adenocarcinoma and 80% had received prior
chemotherapy. Body weight was not tabulated for this cohort; the trial
simulations resampled weight from a previous alectinib NSCLC cohort (median
77.5 kg, range 49-123 kg).

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("vanderHeijden_2023_alectinib")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment in
`inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/vanderHeijden_2023_alectinib.R`. All values are
in Data S1 Table S2, which the article reproduces from the EMA assessment
report (structural and IIV estimates) plus the two simulation assumptions
marked with an asterisk there (fasted bioavailability and IOV).

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL/F at 70 kg) | log(81.9 L/h) | Table S2 'Cl/F'; $THETA(1) |
| `lvc` (V/F at 70 kg) | log(4016 L) | Table S2 'V/F'; $THETA(2) |
| `lka` | log(1.30 1/h) | Table S2 'Ka'; $THETA(3) |
| `ld1` (zero-order input duration) | log(3.44 h) | Table S2 'D1'; $THETA(4) |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_vc` | 0.75, 1 (fixed) | Methods 'Population pharmacokinetic model'; Data S1 code TVCL / TVV |
| `lfdepot` (F with food) | log(1) (fixed) | Table S2 'F (fed conditions)'; $THETA(5) 1 FIX |
| `lfdepot_fasted` (F fasted) | log(0.714) (fixed) | Table S2 'F (fasted conditions)'; Methods |
| `etalcl`, `etalvc` block | 0.162, 0.07865012, 0.161 | Table S2 IIV rows and covariance; $OMEGA BLOCK(2) |
| `etalka`, `etald1` | 0.398, 0.178 | Table S2 'IIV Ka', 'IIV D1' |
| `etaiov_fdepot_1`, `etaiov_fdepot_2` | 0.0064 each (fixed) | Table S2 'IOV'; $OMEGA BLOCK(1) + BLOCK(1) SAME |
| `propSd` | 0.19 | Table S2 'Proportional error' = 0.0361 (variance) |
| CL, V allometry `(WT/70)^e` | n/a | Data S1 code `TVCL = THETA(1)*(WT/70)**0.75`, `TVV = THETA(2)*(WT/70)**1` |
| F by prandial state and occasion | n/a | Data S1 code `F1=THETA(5)*EXP(ETA(OCC_F1))`; `IF(FLAG.EQ.1) F1=THETA(6)*EXP(ETA(OCC_F1))` |
| Sequential zero-order then first-order absorption | n/a | Methods; Data S1 `ADVAN2 TRANS2` with `D1` |
| `Cc ~ prop(propSd)` | n/a | Data S1 `$ERROR Y = F*(1+EPS(1))+EPS(2)` with EPS(2) 0 FIX |

# Typical-value checks

Doses go into `depot` with `rate = -2`, so the dose enters the depot at a
constant rate over the modelled duration `D1` before first-order absorption.

```{r typical}
mod <- readModelDb("vanderHeijden_2023_alectinib")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

typ_events <- function(amt, fed, occ, id) {
  tibble(
    id = id,
    time = c(0, seq(0, 480, by = 0.25)),
    evid = c(1L, rep(0L, length(seq(0, 480, by = 0.25)))),
    amt = c(amt, rep(0, length(seq(0, 480, by = 0.25)))),
    rate = c(-2, rep(0, length(seq(0, 480, by = 0.25)))),
    cmt = "depot",
    WT = 70,
    FED = fed,
    OCC = occ
  )
}

ev_typ <- bind_rows(
  typ_events(0.1, fed = 1, occ = 1, id = 1L) |> mutate(prandial = "Fed"),
  typ_events(0.1, fed = 0, occ = 2, id = 2L) |> mutate(prandial = "Fasted")
)
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_typ, events = ev_typ, keep = "prandial", rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12
) |>
  as.data.frame()

auc_trap <- function(t, y) sum(diff(t) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)
typ_summary <- sim_typ |>
  group_by(prandial) |>
  summarise(
    cmax_pg = 1000 * max(Cc),
    tmax = time[which.max(Cc)],
    auc = auc_trap(time, Cc),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
auc_fed <- typ_summary$auc[typ_summary$prandial == "Fed"]
auc_fasted <- typ_summary$auc[typ_summary$prandial == "Fasted"]
fe_typ <- 100 * (auc_fed - auc_fasted) / auc_fasted
t_half <- log(2) * 4016 / 81.9

typ_summary |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Prandial state" = prandial,
    "Cmax (pg/mL)" = cmax_pg,
    "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "AUC0-480 (ng*h/mL)" = auc
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 3,
    caption = "Typical 70-kg patient, single 100 ug microtracer dose."
  )
```

For a typical 70-kg patient the model gives:

* a food effect of `r round(fe_typ, 2)`% on AUC, the 40% the authors
  defined as minimally clinically relevant (Equation 1,
  FE = (1 - 0.714)/0.714 = 40%);
* a terminal half-life of log(2) x V/CL = `r round(t_half, 1)` h, close to
  the 32 h the article cites for alectinib;
* Tmax of `r typ_summary$tmax[typ_summary$prandial == "Fed"]` h, inside the 4-6 h
  window the article uses to place its absorption-phase samples;
* a fed microtracer Cmax of about `r round(typ_summary$cmax_pg[typ_summary$prandial == "Fed"])` pg/mL, the
  'pg/mL' range the Methods give as the reason the additive error was dropped.

```{r typical-checks}
stopifnot(
  # Food effect is fixed by construction; the solve reproduces the 40%
  # through F1 = 1 fed vs 0.714 fasted (tolerance covers the 480 h window).
  abs(fe_typ - 40.06) < 0.1,
  # AUC equals F * Dose / CL (dose in mg -> ng/mL via the x1000).
  abs(auc_fed / (0.1 * 1000 / 81.9) - 1) < 0.01,
  all(typ_summary$tmax >= 4 & typ_summary$tmax <= 6),
  abs(t_half - 32) / 32 < 0.1
)
```

# Therapeutic steady state

The microtracer is given on top of the patients' 600 mg twice-daily alectinib
taken with food. The proposed design requires at least 7 days of treatment
before the first microtracer dose, which is about five half-lives.

```{r steady-state}
ev_ss <- rxode2::et(amt = 600, ii = 12, addl = 27, cmt = "depot", rate = -2) |>
  rxode2::et(seq(0, 336, by = 0.5)) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(WT = 70, FED = 1, OCC = 0)

sim_ss <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = ev_ss) |> as.data.frame()

troughs <- sim_ss |> filter(time %in% seq(12, 336, by = 12))
frac_ss_day7 <- troughs$Cc[troughs$time == 168] / troughs$Cc[troughs$time == 336]
stopifnot(frac_ss_day7 > 0.9, frac_ss_day7 < 1)

ggplot(sim_ss, aes(time / 24, Cc)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 7, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (days)",
    y = "Alectinib Cc (ng/mL)",
    title = "Typical 70-kg patient, alectinib 600 mg twice daily with food",
    caption = "Dashed line: day 7, the minimum treatment duration before the microtracer study."
  )
```

The day-7 trough is `r round(100 * frac_ss_day7, 1)`% of the day-14 trough.

# Virtual cohort and proposed study design

The proposed design (Figure 1c) gives the microtracer with food on study day
1 (`OCC = 1`, `FED = 1`) and fasted on study day 9 (`OCC = 2`, `FED = 0`), with
samples at predose and 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 and 24 h after each
microtracer dose. One trial has 10 patients; 20 trials (200 patients) are
simulated here. Body weight is drawn from a log-normal centred on the
article's resampling cohort median (77.5 kg) and truncated to its 49-123 kg
range.

The random effects are drawn in base R and passed to the typical-value model
through `params`, so the cohort is identical on every machine and the same
patient carries the same between-subject random effects on both occasions.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20231012)
n_trials <- 20L
n_per_trial <- 10L
n_sub <- n_trials * n_per_trial

omega <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)$omega
eta <- matrix(rnorm(n_sub * nrow(omega)), n_sub) %*% chol(omega)
colnames(eta) <- rownames(omega)

wt <- exp(rnorm(n_sub * 3, log(77.5), 0.2))
wt <- head(wt[wt >= 49 & wt <= 123], n_sub)
stopifnot(length(wt) == n_sub)

subjects <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  trial = rep(seq_len(n_trials), each = n_per_trial),
  WT = wt
)
params <- data.frame(id = subjects$id, eta)

sample_times <- c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 24)
design_events <- bind_rows(
  # Day 1: microtracer with food
  subjects |> mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = 0.1, rate = -2, FED = 1, OCC = 1),
  subjects |> tidyr::expand_grid(time = sample_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0, FED = 1, OCC = 1),
  # Day 9: microtracer fasted
  subjects |> mutate(time = 192, evid = 1L, amt = 0.1, rate = -2, FED = 0, OCC = 2),
  subjects |> tidyr::expand_grid(time = 192 + sample_times[-1]) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0, FED = 0, OCC = 2)
) |>
  mutate(cmt = "depot") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim_design <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_typ, events = design_events, params = params, keep = "trial"
) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(
    occasion = ifelse(OCC == 1, "Day 1, fed", "Day 9, fasted"),
    tad = ifelse(OCC == 1, time, time - 192)
  )
```

```{r figure-design}
# Proposed design of Figure 1c: microtracer concentration-time profiles on
# the two sampling days (individual predictions, 200 patients).
sim_design |>
  group_by(occasion, tad) |>
  summarise(
    Q10 = quantile(1000 * Cc, 0.1),
    Q50 = quantile(1000 * Cc, 0.5),
    Q90 = quantile(1000 * Cc, 0.9),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, Q50, colour = occasion, fill = occasion)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q10, ymax = Q90), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after microtracer dose (h)",
    y = "Alectinib-d6 Cc (pg/mL)",
    colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
    title = "Microtracer profiles under the proposed study design",
    caption = "Median and 10th-90th percentiles; sampling times of Figure 1c."
  )
```

The day-9 predose sample is not zero: about 2% of the day-1 microtracer
remains after the 8-day washout (5.6 half-lives). The article's popPK
analysis models both doses together, so the carry-over is accounted for; the
NCA below avoids it by solving each occasion as a separate single dose.

# PKNCA validation

The article reports no NCA. Its central quantity is the food effect, which
under linear PK equals the ratio of dose-normalised AUCs in the same patient.
Each patient is therefore solved twice as a single microtracer dose, once fed
on occasion 1 and once fasted on occasion 2, with the same between-subject
random effects and that occasion's IOV random effect. AUC0-inf is computed by
PKNCA per patient and occasion, and the food effect per patient is
FE = AUC(fed) / AUC(fasted) - 1.

```{r pknca}
nca_times <- c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 24, 36, 48, 72, 96, 120, 168, 240)
single_dose <- function(fed, occ, offset) {
  bind_rows(
    subjects |> mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = 0.1, rate = -2),
    subjects |> tidyr::expand_grid(time = nca_times) |>
      mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0)
  ) |>
    mutate(
      subject = id, id = id + offset, cmt = "depot", FED = fed, OCC = occ,
      treatment = ifelse(fed == 1, "Fed", "Fasted")
    ) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}
nca_events <- bind_rows(
  single_dose(fed = 1, occ = 1, offset = 0L),
  single_dose(fed = 0, occ = 2, offset = n_sub)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(nca_events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

nca_params <- bind_rows(params, params |> mutate(id = id + n_sub))
sim_nca <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_typ, events = nca_events, params = nca_params,
  keep = c("subject", "trial", "treatment")
) |>
  as.data.frame()

conc_df <- sim_nca |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, subject, trial, treatment, time, Cc)
dose_df <- nca_events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, subject, trial, treatment, time, amt)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, id, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

nca_wide |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(
    cmax_pg = 1000 * median(cmax),
    tmax = median(tmax),
    aucinf = median(aucinf.obs),
    half_life = median(half.life),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Prandial state" = treatment,
    "Median Cmax (pg/mL)" = cmax_pg,
    "Median Tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "Median AUC0-inf (ng*h/mL)" = aucinf,
    "Median half-life (h)" = half_life
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "PKNCA results, single 100 ug microtracer dose (200 patients).")
```

## Comparison against published values

The only NCA-type value the article states for alectinib is its 32 h
half-life (cited from the literature, not computed by the article).

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~half.life,
  "Fed", 32,
  "Fasted", 32
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated vs. published half-life. * differs from reference by >20%.")
```

## Food effect per trial

The article's base design (10 patients, food effect 40%, IOV 8%) estimated a
mean food effect of 39.8% with an 80% interval of 31.0%-48.6% over 1000
NONMEM re-estimations (Results, 'Feasibility study'). The NCA analogue below
takes the geometric-mean AUC ratio of each simulated 10-patient trial.

```{r food-effect}
fe_subject <- nca_wide |>
  dplyr::mutate(subject = ifelse(treatment == "Fed", id, id - n_sub)) |>
  dplyr::select(subject, treatment, aucinf.obs) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = treatment, values_from = aucinf.obs) |>
  dplyr::left_join(subjects |> dplyr::select(subject = id, trial), by = "subject") |>
  dplyr::mutate(log_ratio = log(Fed / Fasted))

fe_trial <- fe_subject |>
  group_by(trial) |>
  summarise(fe = 100 * (exp(mean(log_ratio)) - 1), .groups = "drop")

fe_table <- tibble(
  Source = c("van der Heijden 2023 (popPK SSE, 1000 trials)", "This simulation (NCA, 20 trials)"),
  `Mean FE (%)` = c(39.8, mean(fe_trial$fe)),
  `10th percentile (%)` = c(31.0, unname(quantile(fe_trial$fe, 0.1))),
  `90th percentile (%)` = c(48.6, unname(quantile(fe_trial$fe, 0.9)))
)
knitr::kable(fe_table, digits = 1, caption = "Estimated food effect per 10-patient trial.")

stopifnot(
  nrow(fe_subject) == n_sub,
  # Centre: a reversed FED coding gives about -29%, a missing F1 effect 0%.
  abs(mean(fe_trial$fe) - 40) < 4,
  # Per-patient ratio spread comes from IOV alone: sd(log ratio) is
  # sqrt(2 * 0.0064) = 0.113; dropping or doubling the IOV moves it far
  # outside this window.
  abs(sd(fe_subject$log_ratio) - 0.113) < 0.03
)
```

The NCA food effect is centred on 40%, as the article's estimate is. Its
interval is narrower because the NCA uses noise-free individual predictions
on a rich schedule, so the only source of spread is the 8% IOV; the article's
interval also carries the 19% proportional residual error and the uncertainty
of estimating the food effect from 10 sparse profiles.

# Assumptions and deviations

* The article fitted no model of its own. The structural parameters and IIV
  are the EMA Alecensa assessment-report estimates as reproduced in the
  article's Data S1 Table S2; the EMA report itself was not consulted.
* The fasted bioavailability (0.714) and the IOV variance (0.0064, 8% CV) are
  design assumptions of the simulation, not estimates, and are fixed in the
  model. The article's sensitivity analyses vary them (food effect 20-40%, IOV
  8-27%); to explore those scenarios, override `lfdepot_fasted` and the two
  `etaiov_fdepot_*` variances with `ini()`.
* The EMA model's additive residual error was set to 0 by the authors because
  the microtracer concentrations (pg/mL) are far below the therapeutic range;
  it is omitted here and its EMA value is not reported in the article. For
  therapeutic alectinib concentrations the model therefore lacks the additive
  component of the original EMA model.
* The article assumes the microtracer (alectinib-d6) has the same PK as
  alectinib, so the model describes both. Its metabolite M4 is not modelled.
* The paper's `FLAG` column (1 = fasted occasion) is encoded as `FED = 1 - FLAG`.
  Doses must use `rate = -2` so the modelled duration `D1` is applied.
* The covariance of the CL/F and V/F random effects uses the unrounded
  value in the Data S1 NONMEM code (0.07865012) rather than Table S2's 0.0787.
* Body weight for the virtual cohort is drawn from a truncated log-normal
  matched to the article's resampling cohort (median 77.5 kg, range 49-123
  kg); the individual weights used by the authors are not published.
* The article's power analysis (Figures 3-4, S1-S3) requires repeated NONMEM
  estimation and is not reproduced; the food-effect summary above is an NCA
  analogue of its base design.
* No erratum or correction notice for this article was found as of
  2026-10-28.
